questions.prompt: What is a closure, and how does it explain both the makeCounter factory and the var-in-a-loop trap?

keyPoints.text: The inner function keeps access to count after makeCounter has finished running; that preserved access is closure.
keyPoints.quote: still has access to `count` even after `makeCounter` finishes running. That preserved access is closure.

keyPoints.text: Every call to makeCounter creates a new count, so two counters do not share state.
Nothing outside can read or reset count, so closures are a simple way to keep data private.
keyPoints.quote: Nothing outside can read or reset `count` directly, which is why closures are also a simple way to keep data private.

keyPoints.text: With var there is a single i for the whole function, so every closure sees its final value.
keyPoints.quote: With `var`, there is one `i` for the whole function, and every closure sees its final value, `3`.

keyPoints.text: With let each loop iteration gets its own binding, so the closures return 0, 1, 2.
keyPoints.quote: With `let`, each loop iteration gets its own `j`.

keyPoints.text: Closures are why a bug in a callback can depend on variables declared much earlier.
keyPoints.quote: This is why a bug inside a callback can depend on variables that were declared much earlier.

questions.prompt: Why does the lesson push you to keep decision logic pure and side effects at the edges?

keyPoints.text: A pure function's output depends only on its inputs and it changes nothing outside itself.
keyPoints.quote: A function is **pure** when its output depends only on its inputs and it changes nothing outside itself.

keyPoints.text: A side effect is any change the caller can observe besides the return value, such as mutating shared objects, writing to the screen or storage, or sending requests.
keyPoints.quote: A **side effect** is any change the caller can observe besides the return value

keyPoints.text: Side effects are not bad in themselves; apps exist to cause them.
keyPoints.quote: Side effects are not bad. Apps exist to cause them.

keyPoints.text: Pure logic is easy to test and reuse, so the skill is confining effects to a few obvious places.
keyPoints.quote: keeping the decision-making logic pure, because pure logic is easy to test and reuse

keyPoints.text: addToCartTotal gives a different result each call because it depends on hidden state, while withItemAdded(0, 10) always gives 10.
keyPoints.quote: Calling `addToCartTotal(10)` twice gives a different result each time because it depends on hidden state.

keyPoints.text: In review, ask whether a function has a side effect its name hides.
keyPoints.quote: "Does this function have a side effect the name hides?"

questions.prompt: How do you choose and use array methods safely, and which of them can surprise the caller?

keyPoints.text: Pick the method by the question you are asking: map transforms, filter keeps some, find gives the first match, some/every answer yes-or-no, reduce combines.
keyPoints.quote: Pick the method by the question you are asking

keyPoints.text: filter returns a new array and leaves the original unchanged.
keyPoints.quote: `filter` returns a new array containing only matching items. It does not change the original array.

keyPoints.text: reduce needs a starting value, otherwise it throws on an empty array.
keyPoints.quote: Always give `reduce` a starting value (the `0`); without it, `reduce` on an empty array throws a `TypeError`.

keyPoints.text: push, pop, splice, reverse and sort change the array in place.
keyPoints.quote: `push`, `pop`, `splice`, `reverse`, and `sort` change the array in place.

keyPoints.text: sort() without a comparator compares items as strings, so 100 sorts before 9.
keyPoints.quote: `sort()` with no comparator compares items as **strings**

keyPoints.text: Copy before you sort or reverse unless changing the original is the point.
keyPoints.quote: Copy before you sort or reverse, unless changing the original is the point.

keyPoints.text: find returns one item or undefined, so check for undefined before reading properties.
keyPoints.quote: It returns one item or `undefined`. Check for `undefined` before reading properties.
